{{2020–21 Mid-American Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2020–21 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team''' represented the [[University at Buffalo]] in the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bulls, led by second-year head coach [[Jim Whitesell]], played their home games at [[Alumni Arena (University at Buffalo)|Alumni Arena]] in [[Amherst, New York]] as members of the [[Mid-American Conference]]. Starting this season, the MAC announced the removal of divisions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mid-american-conference-cancels-postseason-tournaments-for-eight-sports-changes-basketball-format/|title=Mid-American Conference cancels postseason tournaments for eight sports, changes basketball format|work=CBSSports.com|date=May 12, 2020|accessdate=January 28, 2021|language=en}}</ref> They finished the season 16–9, 12–5 in MAC play to finish in second place. They defeated [[2020–21 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami (OH)]] and [[2020–21 Akron Zips men's basketball team|Akron]] to advance to the championship game of the [[2021 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] where they lost to [[2020–21 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]]. They were invited to the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2020–21 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]].

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Bulls]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 20–12, 11–7 in MAC play to finish in third place in the MAC East division. They were upset in the first round of the [[2020 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] by [[2019–20 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami (OH)]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2020/03/mens-basketball-season-ends-after-home-loss-to-miami-oh|title=Men's basketball season ends after home loss to Miami (OH)|work=The Spectrum|date=March 10, 2020|accessdate=January 28, 2021|language=en}}</ref>
